tasks.short: Collect interval meter data, analyse the peak demand profile, inspect the building management system and equipment on site, judge feasibility, and write the feasibility note.

steps.what: Client gives consent for the meter data link
Energy auditor collects interval meter data: as files from the client by e-mail today, through the data link after the change
Energy auditor analyses peak demand periods in spreadsheets
Energy auditor examines commercial sites and the building management system
Energy auditor determines the feasibility of installing demand control equipment
Energy auditor writes the feasibility note

tasks.design: With the client's consent, quarter-hour meter data come through a data link from the grid operator instead of files by e-mail. Code finds the peak periods, their timing and the loads running then, and shows them on a dashboard ({BI}). The feasibility note template carries the load profile charts. Examining the site and its building management system and judging feasibility stay with the auditor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meter files arrived by e-mail and peaks were found in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Meter data links with consent; load profile analysis in code.
tasks.still_hard: Older building management systems cannot take control signals.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which loads a hotel can really shift without guests noticing.
tasks.altitude: The auditor judges sites instead of building spreadsheets.

evidence.claim: Ella Energy reads three years of quarter-hour meter data, predicts normal use and flags deviations.
Meter readings are personal data, open only to grid operator and supplier without consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the site request to the feasibility note; installation is outside.
Input contract: client consent for the meter data link; fallback is e-mailed files.

Site examination and judgement keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for checking the data link and gaps. s2 keeps 40 for reading the peaks and the loads behind them. s5 keeps 70 because the charts fill in but the auditor still writes the note.
Clients give consent (s0, share 1) in about the time sending files took; this is outside the auditor's savings.
research_questions: Do code-found peaks match what the site visit shows?

incremental.description: Energy auditor arranges data consent with each client.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: sites without interval data or consent, so files come by e-mail and peaks are found by hand (10.9); high: sites with years of interval data through the link (26.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate savings and payback per measure, select measures, write the advice report, check it, send it to the client, and explain the recommendations.

steps.what: Energy auditor calculates savings and payback per measure in spreadsheets
Energy auditor selects energy-efficient technologies or alternate energy sources to recommend
Energy auditor writes the advice report

loop.input: The selected measures with quantities, savings and payback from the calculation, and site notes.
loop.output: A draft report: tables filled from the calculation and a narrative per measure.
loop.check: Code checks every number in the narrative against the calculation output and drops sentences that do not match. The auditor reads each drafted paragraph against the selected measure and the site findings: it must describe the measure, its limits and its assumptions as they are; unclear text is rewritten by the auditor.
loop.stop: One draft per report; if the check drops more than a few sentences, the auditor writes the narrative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Clients need each measure explained for their building; tables alone do not persuade.

steps.what: Energy auditor checks the final report: measures, numbers and narrative say what was found and selected, and it goes to this client
Energy auditor sends the checked and signed report to the client: by e-mail today, by one send from the calculation tool after the change
Energy auditor explains the recommendations to the client

tasks.design: A calculation tool holds the recognised measures list, tariffs and weather data as configuration and computes savings and payback per measure, instead of a new spreadsheet per audit. The report fills its tables from the calculation, and a bounded step drafts the narrative per measure; code checks every number against the calculation, and the auditor edits and signs. The auditor checks the final report and sends it to the client. Selecting measures and explaining them stay with the auditor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Savings were calculated in a new spreadsheet each time and reports written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Measure lists and tariffs can be configured; models draft narratives that code checks.
tasks.still_hard: Clients act on cash flow, not payback.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the first measure a hesitant owner will actually take.
tasks.altitude: The auditor selects and explains instead of calculating and writing.

reach.learn: Whether more recommended measures are carried out.

evidence.claim: OptiMiser calibrates its building model against utility bills and writes customer-ready reports.
Firms report energy measures every four years against the recognised measures list.

assumptions: Boundary: from audit data to the client informed; installation is outside.
Input contract: measures list and tariffs kept current; fallback is spreadsheets.

The auditor signs every report; selecting, checking and explaining keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 for entering site data and checking results. s3 keeps 60 because tables fill in and the auditor reads and edits every paragraph. s5 keeps 20 for the send.
research_questions: Do clients carry out more recommended measures?

incremental.description: Energy auditor updates tariffs and the measures list.

approvals.approved_version: The signed advice report exactly as checked by the auditor in s4, sent once to the client named on the audit; any change needs a new check and signature.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual buildings with custom measures outside the list, so many savings are still calculated and written by hand (16.2); high: standard offices and shops (31.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather bills and meter readings, record field observations, download and merge logger data, normalise usage for weather and analyse patterns, and interpret them.

steps.what: Client gives consent for the meter data link
Energy auditor gathers bills and meter readings: by e-mail from the client today, through the data link after the change
Energy auditor collects field data on equipment: on paper today, in tablet forms per equipment type with photos after the change
Energy auditor downloads logger data and merges it in spreadsheets
Energy auditor analyzes energy usage for weather and patterns
Energy auditor interprets the usage patterns

tasks.design: With consent, meter data come through a data link instead of bills by e-mail. Field observations go into tablet forms per equipment type with photos. Logger files are imported by a script and merged with meter data on time stamps, and degree-day regression and load profiles are computed in code and shown on a dashboard ({BI}). Interpreting the patterns stays with the auditor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bills, notes and logger files were merged by hand in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Meter data links, logger import scripts and degree-day analysis in code.
tasks.still_hard: Scanned bills from small suppliers need reading.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising that a weekend spike is a cleaning crew, not a fault.
tasks.altitude: The auditor interprets patterns instead of merging files.

evidence.claim: Ella Energy predicts normal use from quarter-hour meter data and flags deviations.
Meter readings are personal data, open only to grid operator and supplier without consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the audit start to patterns interpreted; recommendations are outside.
Input contract: client consent and loggers with exportable files; fallback is bills and spreadsheets.

Interpreting patterns stays with the auditor at full time. s2 keeps 90 because the auditor still records each observation; only equipment headings fill in. s3 keeps 40 for checking imports and gaps; typing field notes later goes. s4 keeps 40 for reading the computed results.
Clients give consent (s0, share 1) in about the time sending bills took; this is outside the auditor's savings.
research_questions: Do merged data sets have fewer gaps?

incremental.description: Energy auditor keeps import scripts working for new logger types.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few loggers with export and paper bills, so most data are still gathered and merged by hand (27.0); high: many loggers with interval meter data (42.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Install data loggers and take spot measurements, write readings down, retrieve loggers, and file readings.

steps.what: Energy auditor measures energy usage with data loggers, light meters, amp probes and flue gas analyzers
Energy auditor writes readings on paper sheets
Energy auditor retrieves loggers and downloads their data
Energy auditor files the readings for the audit

tasks.design: Instruments with a wireless link send spot readings straight into the tablet form for the measuring point, so readings are not written on paper and typed later. Logger files are attached to the audit record ({OPS_SYSTEM}) on download. Taking measurements and handling loggers stay with the auditor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were written on paper sheets and typed in later.
tasks.enabler_now: Measuring instruments with wireless links send readings to tablets.
tasks.still_hard: Older instruments have no data link.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing where to clamp an amp probe safely in a crowded panel.

reach.learn: Whether readings arrive without typing errors.

evidence.claim: Measuring instruments with wireless links can send readings to tablet forms.

assumptions: Boundary: from the measurement plan to readings filed; analysis is outside.
Input contract: instruments with data links; fallback is paper.

incremental.description: Energy auditor pairs instruments with the tablet.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older instruments without a link, so most readings are still written and typed (5.5); high: connected instruments for most points (13.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The energy auditor keeps examining sites, measuring, selecting and explaining measures; e-mailed files, spreadsheet merging, calculations and paper readings shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An auditor with more time on site and with clients.
